blueprint.title: ELF Section Integrity Validator Repair
blueprint.scenario: You maintain a small in-house firmware validation toolchain (~1200 lines across 6 files) that verifies ELF binaries before they are flashed to embedded targets. The toolchain ships as a mix of Python scripts and a compiled C extension (`elfcheck.so`) that performs the inner checksum math. QA recently flagged that certain firmware builds pass validation but fail on-device — the validator is silently accepting corrupt binaries under specific conditions that only appear in production ELFs with unusual section layouts.
blueprint.instruction_draft: Hey, the firmware validator in /app is clearing binaries that blow up on device. QA says it happens with ELFs that have sections aligned to large boundaries or with SHT_NOBITS sections mixed in. Run some of the test ELFs in /app/test_vectors and you'll see the validator claims they're clean. Fix it so every section's stored checksum actually matches its content, and add a standalone verifier script at /app/verify_elf.py that reads any ELF file and exits 0 only if all checkable sections pass — exit 1 with a human-readable error otherwise. The existing /app/validate.py CLI must still work and must now correctly reject the bad test vectors.
requirements: A standalone script /app/verify_elf.py that reads an ELF file path from argv[1] and exits 0 if all SHT_PROGBITS and SHT_INIT_ARRAY sections have valid checksums, exits 1 with a descriptive message otherwise
The existing /app/validate.py CLI must correctly reject ELF test vectors in /app/test_vectors/ that are marked as corrupt (those with filenames containing 'bad')
The existing /app/validate.py CLI must correctly accept ELF test vectors marked as good (filenames containing 'good')
Checksum validation must correctly handle SHT_NOBITS sections (e.g. .bss) by skipping them entirely rather than treating them as zero-filled
Checksum validation must correctly handle sections with sh_addralign > 4096 by using sh_offset (file offset) rather than sh_addr for locating section data

The checksum algorithm must match the specification in /app/docs/checksum_spec.md exactly: Fletcher-32 over 16-bit words in little-endian order, with proper handling of odd-length sections via zero-padding of the final byte
verify_elf.py must work correctly on freshly generated ELF files not present in /app/test_vectors/
environment: Dockerfile FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm; apt-get install gcc binutils-dev; pip install pyelftools==0.31
/app/docs/checksum_spec.md: complete Fletcher-32 spec for firmware sections, 16-bit words LE, odd-length zero-pad, section types to check (SHT_PROGBITS, SHT_INIT_ARRAY), skip SHT_NOBITS

/app/elfcheck.so: compiled C extension (source NOT present) that exports compute_checksum(data: bytes) -> int; it has a silent bug: it uses sh_addr instead of sh_offset when the caller passes the raw ELF bytes and a section index, BUT the compute_checksum(data) function itself is correct — the bug is in the Python glue code that calls it

/app/elfcheck_glue.py: Python wrapper (~80 lines) that loads elfcheck.so via ctypes and calls compute_checksum; bug 1: uses elf_section.sh_addr as the file seek offset (should be sh_addr... wait, sh_offset), bug 2: for SHT_NOBITS sections it reads sh_size zero bytes from the file instead of skipping
/app/validate.py: main CLI (~150 lines) that calls elfcheck_glue.compute_and_compare() for each section; passes currently because test vectors were generated with the buggy glue
/app/section_store.py: section metadata cache (~120 lines), correct but complex, not involved in the bug
/app/elf_loader.py: ELF parsing wrapper around pyelftools (~200 lines), correct
/app/config.py: configuration and thresholds (~90 lines), not involved

/app/test_vectors/: 8 pre-built ELF files; 4 named good_*.elf (validator should accept), 4 named bad_*.elf (validator should reject); the good ones have correct Fletcher-32 checksums in a custom PT_NOTE segment; the bad ones have intentionally wrong checksums; because of the dual bugs in elfcheck_glue.py, validate.py currently ACCEPTS all 8

test_vectors include: good_aligned.elf (normal), good_nobits.elf (has .bss), good_large_align.elf (sh_addralign=65536), good_mixed.elf (multiple section types); bad_corrupt_text.elf, bad_corrupt_data.elf, bad_corrupt_init.elf, bad_large_align_corrupt.elf
ELF test vectors are generated by a build script /app/tools/make_test_vectors.py that is present and runnable, showing the correct checksums for reference

The checksum is stored in a custom PT_NOTE segment with name 'FWCHECK' and type 1, one descriptor per section (section index as namesz, checksum as 4-byte LE descsz payload) — this structure is documented in checksum_spec.md
Verifier tests at verify time generate fresh ELF files using make_test_vectors.py with new random section contents and known-correct checksums, then test verify_elf.py against them
blueprint.internal_hint: The difficulty is observe_not_read: the bugs are in elfcheck_glue.py in how it calls the .so, not in the .so itself. Bug 1 is that elfcheck_glue.py reads section data using `section.header.sh_addr` as the file seek position instead of `section.header.sh_offset` — for most normal ELFs these happen to be equal (or close enough that the test vectors were built to pass), but for sections with large alignment or when ASLR shifts addresses, they diverge. Bug 2 is that for SHT_NOBITS sections, the code does `f.seek(sh_offset); f.read(sh_size)` and feeds the bytes to compute_checksum, rather than skipping. The solver must run the test ELFs and observe that validate.py incorrectly accepts bad vectors, then instrument elfcheck_glue.py to print intermediate values and compare against the spec in checksum_spec.md to discover the two wrong field references. The .so source is absent so the solver cannot just read it — they must trust that compute_checksum(bytes)->int is correct and isolate the glue bugs. The fix requires understanding the ELF section header fields (sh_offset vs sh_addr vs sh_addralign) and implementing the Fletcher-32 spec cleanly in verify_elf.py independently of the glue code.
blueprint.trap: A naive agent that reads elfcheck_glue.py will see reasonable-looking code (sh_addr is a legitimate field name) and may not notice the offset/address confusion without running the large-align test vector and observing a wrong result. Agents that fix only the SHT_NOBITS bug pass the nobits test vector but fail the large-align hidden test. Agents that reuse elfcheck_glue.py in verify_elf.py inherit both bugs. Agents that implement verify_elf.py from scratch but get the Fletcher-32 wrong (e.g. using 32-bit words instead of 16-bit, or not zero-padding odd lengths) pass the visible test vectors (which happen to have even-length sections) but fail hidden ones with odd-length sections.
tests: Run validate.py on each of the 8 pre-built test vectors; assert it rejects all 4 bad_*.elf files and accepts all 4 good_*.elf files
Run verify_elf.py on good_large_align.elf; assert exit 0
Run verify_elf.py on bad_large_align_corrupt.elf; assert exit 1 with non-empty stderr/stdout
Run verify_elf.py on good_nobits.elf; assert exit 0 (SHT_NOBITS sections skipped correctly)

Generate a fresh ELF at verify time with random SHT_PROGBITS section content of odd byte length (17 bytes, 33 bytes) and compute correct Fletcher-32 with zero-padding; run verify_elf.py on it; assert exit 0
Generate a fresh ELF at verify time with the same structure but corrupt the stored checksum by XORing one byte; run verify_elf.py; assert exit 1
Generate a fresh ELF at verify time with sh_addralign=131072 (large alignment forcing sh_offset != sh_addr); verify_elf.py must exit 0 with correct checksum, exit 1 with wrong checksum
Generate a fresh ELF with a SHT_NOBITS section (.bss) between two SHT_PROGBITS sections; verify_elf.py must exit 0 and must NOT attempt to read sh_size bytes for the NOBITS section
Verify that verify_elf.py exits 0 in under 2 seconds on a 512KB ELF (performance sanity check, not a tight bar)

verifier_knob.name: corpus_size
verifier_knob.effect: Increasing adds more edge-case ELFs: sections with size 1 byte, sections with sh_offset=0 (unlikely but valid), ELFs with 20+ sections of mixed types, ELFs where every section has odd length; decreasing to 4 makes it easier to pass by luck

expected_failure_modes: Agent reads elfcheck_glue.py, sees 'sh_addr' and 'sh_offset' both present in the code, does not notice which one is wrong without running the large-align test vector
Agent fixes elfcheck_glue.py but writes verify_elf.py to call the same glue, inheriting the residual bugs
Agent implements Fletcher-32 correctly for even-length sections but forgets zero-padding for odd-length sections, passing all visible test vectors but failing hidden odd-length ones

Agent fixes only the SHT_NOBITS bug (the more obviously wrong one) after observing the nobits test vector fail, ships without noticing the sh_addr/sh_offset bug because good_large_align.elf happens to pass before the fix (due to how the test ELF was laid out)

Agent implements verify_elf.py using 32-bit word Fletcher instead of 16-bit, which produces the same result for sections whose length is a multiple of 4 (all visible test vectors) but fails the hidden 17-byte and 33-byte section tests

speedrun: # Spot sh_addr used as file seek offset (should be sh_offset) — visible in source
# Spot SHT_NOBITS reads sh_size bytes instead of skipping — visible in source
# Edit elfcheck_glue.py: replace sh_addr with sh_offset in file seek call
# Edit elfcheck_glue.py: add SHT_NOBITS skip (continue instead of read+checksum)
for f in /app/test_vectors/*.elf; do python /app/validate.py $f; done  # check all 8
# Write /app/verify_elf.py: parse ELF with pyelftools, implement Fletcher-32 per spec (16-bit words LE, zero-pad odd), skip NOBITS, use sh_offset, read PT_NOTE checksums, compare
invalid_failure_risks: The PT_NOTE checksum storage format (namesz=section_index, descsz=checksum payload) is non-standard and complex; if make_test_vectors.py generates ELFs with a slightly different structure than verify_elf.py expects to parse, tests fail ambiguously

The elfcheck.so binary must be pre-compiled for the exact target architecture in the Docker image; if the build step fails or produces an incompatible .so, the entire task environment is broken before the agent starts

The claim that 'for most normal ELFs sh_addr ≈ sh_offset' may not hold for the pre-built good_*.elf test vectors after applying the fix — if good_large_align.elf was built with the buggy code, fixing the glue might cause it to fail even the 'good' vectors unless the test vectors were built with correct checksums

The speedrun reveals both bugs are directly visible by source-reading (sh_addr vs sh_offset as file seek argument is immediately obviously wrong), contradicting the observe_not_read difficulty lever and capping genuine_difficulty at 2
If pyelftools 0.31 parses PT_NOTE segments differently than the custom FWCHECK note format expects, verify_elf.py implementations that use pyelftools note parsing may silently get wrong checksums
review.reasons: The task fails the genuine_difficulty threshold: both bugs are directly visible by reading elfcheck_glue.py (using sh_addr as a file seek offset is immediately recognizable as wrong to any ELF-literate engineer), making the 'observe_not_read' framing misleading and the speedrun achievable in ~17 commands. The score of 2 on genuine_difficulty falls below the required minimum of 4. Additionally, there is a structural risk that fixing the glue code may break the pre-built 'good' test vectors if those vectors were generated assuming the buggy behavior, creating potential for invalid test failures.
fixes: To increase genuine_difficulty to 4+, make the bugs non-obvious from source: instead of a clearly wrong field name (sh_addr as file seek), hide the bug as an off-by-one in alignment padding calculation, or a subtle integer overflow in Fletcher-32 accumulation that only triggers on specific section sizes — something that reads correctly but computes wrongly

Alternatively, move the primary bug into the compiled elfcheck.so (with source present but complex C), forcing the agent to reason about C pointer arithmetic and byte ordering rather than obvious Python field name confusion

Remove the internal hint's self-contradictory claim that 'sh_addr is a legitimate field name' making it non-obvious — if it's immediately obvious to any ELF engineer, the observe_not_read tag is wrong and the difficulty lever is broken; redesign so the confusion requires actually running test vectors to observe divergence

Ensure test vector ELFs are built with correct checksums (not checksums matching the buggy behavior), so fixing the glue immediately makes good_*.elf pass and bad_*.elf fail without a bootstrapping problem

Add a hidden complication: e.g., the PT_NOTE section for checksums uses a non-obvious alignment rule that pyelftools doesn't expose directly, forcing the agent to implement raw binary parsing rather than relying on library abstractions

verdicts.reason: That task is about creating a polyglot bash/Python validator for YAML config fields, while the candidate is about repairing ELF binary checksum validation with specific handling of section types and alignment.
That task is about a polyglot script validating KEY=VALUE config files, unrelated to ELF binary format, checksum algorithms, or firmware validation.
That task is about parsing research paper text files into JSON metadata, completely different domain from ELF binary integrity and checksum validation.

Both tasks involve repairing a silent bug in a cryptographic/checksum computation within a multi-file toolchain where the existing tests pass but production data fails — the core problem structure (find and fix a subtle correctness bug in byte-level data processing) is essentially the same, differing mainly in domain (AES-CTR vs. Fletcher-32 over ELF sections).
That task is about fixing NetFlow v9 binary parsing and per-counterparty aggregation logic, a different domain and problem structure from ELF section checksum validation.
